title: On-call Rotation Design, SLA Blitz Kit, and Incident Communication Templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page consolidates the operational on-call rotation policy, a pre-packed SLA Blitz Kit for rapid stabilization, runbook excerpts for the most frequent incident classes, a game-day schedule for sim exercises, and customer/status-page communication templates. The goal is a single, actionable reference for first responders and bridge operators to reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to restore (MTTR) while preserving consistent customer messaging.

Audience:
- Primary: SREs, on-call engineers, on-call rotation coordinators.
- Secondary: Product incident liaisons, Customer Success, Legal (for high-severity customer notifications).

Ownership and escalation:
- Runbook owner: Platform Reliability (team: eng-sre).
- On-call coordinator: Rotation Ops (team: eng-sre).
- Pager escalation matrix: See section \"Escalation Matrix (quick view)\" below.

SLOs and alerting thresholds (applies to Redwood API surface):
| Metric | Target (monthly) | Alert threshold | Severity classification |
|--------|------------------:|----------------:|-------------------------:|
| API 95th latency (text-generate, p50-1s context) | <= 1200 ms | > 1600 ms for 10m | Sev3 |
| Request success rate (5xx) | >= 99.90% | <= 99.70% for 5m | Sev2 |
| Streaming disconnect rate | <= 0.5% | > 1.0% for 10m | Sev2 |
| Dedicated pool capacity utilization | <= 85% | >= 95% for 15m | Capacity |

Note: For customer-impacting degradation that crosses a legal/regulatory boundary (e.g., Private deployment data residency incidents), automatically classify as Sev1 and involve Security & Legal.

On-call rotation rules (practical policy):
1) Rotation cadence: 7-day primary shifts, 14-day secondary on-call with 48-hour handover overlap on rotations flagged as \"holiday-sensitive\".
2) Shift coverage: Primary is responsible for initial acknowledgement and remediation. Secondary is responsible for escalation and weekend follow-through.
3) Working hours: Primary must acknowledge pages within 10 minutes during shift window; secondary must respond to escalations within 30 minutes.
4) Handovers: Each handover includes a 15-minute synchronous overlap with an anchor note posted to the rotation channel and a brief on-call checklist run.
5) Protected time: One team member per rotation may opt out for up to 2 days for personal reasons with at least 72 hours notice; coordinator approves exceptions.

On-call playbook (first 20 minutes):
- Step 0: Acknowledge the page in the paging tool (PagerDuty / Opsgenie) and post an \"I am investigating\" message to #oncall-bridge.
- Step 1 (0–3m): Collect signal summary: affected service, region, approximate impact, recent deploys (last 30m), and any ongoing maintenance windows.
  - Command examples: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-platform -o wide --selector=service=api`
  - Query APM: `latency > 1.6s` dashboard link (embed).
- Step 2 (3–8m): Run containment checks: scale up dedicated pool by +1 replica policy, enable automatic fallback routing to regional replica. Commands: `redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-us-west --add 1 --reason \"oncall scale\"`
- Step 3 (8–15m): If customer-facing errors are present, open incident bridge with template \"SEV2_BRIDGE\" and notify Customer Success with initial impact estimate.
- Step 4 (15–20m): Decide severity and whether to trigger P1/P2 procedures. If Sev1, call the incident commander (IC) and request cross-functional bridge.

Escalation Matrix (quick view):
- Primary on-call -> after 10 min with no acknowledgement escalates to Secondary -> after 20 additional minutes escalates to Team Lead -> if still unresolved after 60 minutes, page Incident Commander (rotating exec duty).
- Security issues: Primary -> Security on-call (immediate) -> Legal (within 30 minutes).

SLA Blitz Kit (checklist to stabilize a customer-impacting incident):
1) Communications (first 15m):
  - Post a one-line status to the internal incident channel and create a public status-page draft (see template below).
  - Notify Customer Success for any customers with dedicated contracts.
2) Technical triage (first 30m):
  - Snapshot service state (API server logs, database replication lag, GPU node health).
  - If degradation from recent deploy, perform a safe rollback: `redwoodctl rollout undo --service api --to-revision REViD` (follow rollback runbook).
  - If sudden capacity starvation, execute emergency autoscale per policy: `redwoodctl autoscale --pool dedicated-us-west --factor 2 --ttl 15m`
3) Containment:
  - Apply rate limiting at the ingress for affected endpoints to prevent cascading failures. Example NGINX config snippet described below.
  - Temporarily route gold-tier customers to a stable model variant to preserve SLAs (see routing policies doc).
4) Stabilization and monitoring:
  - Deploy a short-lived synthetic traffic job to validate fix; run `make smoke-test TARGET=us-west` and observe error-rate metrics for 10 minutes.

Runbook excerpts (three high-frequency incident classes):
1) Latency spike in text generation API
- Symptoms: 95th percentile latency for /v1/generate > 2s, KV-cache miss rate spike, GPU-side memory pressure logs.
- Immediate steps: scale ephemeral workers, bin-pack eviction policy: `memcachedctl evict --service kvcache --age > 5m`.
- Longer-term: increase hot-cache size in provisioning and add additional kernel tuning for attention window.
2) High 5xx rate across multi-region
- Symptoms: > 0.5% 5xx sustained for 5m across regions.
- Immediate steps: pin traffic to unaffected regions, trigger model-fallback to quantized variant with safety net, open a bridge and run the cross-region command: `redwoodctl route set --service api --region eu-central --weight 0.75`.
3) Dedicated pool outage (single-customer)
- Symptoms: customer reports connection timeouts; pool nodes show node failures.
- Immediate steps: failover to reserved warm pool, enable customer-specific fallback route, escalate to Dedicated Support and Account TOC.

Status page and customer communication templates (copy/paste-ready):
- Status page short update (first 30m):
  Title: \"Partial degradation of Redwood API — Generations (US-WEST)\"
  Body: \"We are investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation in US-WEST. Customers may observe increased latencies and occasional 5xx errors. Our engineers have opened an incident bridge and are working on containment. We will post updates every 30 minutes. (Incident ID: {INC_ID})\"

- Customer email template (for named accounts)  — first notification:
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident {INC_ID} — Possible impact to generation latency
  Body:
  Hi {CustomerName},

  We are currently investigating an issue that may be affecting generation latency for requests routed to the US-WEST region. Our engineers have opened a bridge and are applying mitigations. At this time we estimate impact to be limited to {estimated_percentage}% of requests. We will update you within 30 minutes or as we have more information. If you have any time-sensitive workloads, please reply to this message and we will prioritize a route change.

  — Aisha, Platform Reliability

- Full post-incident customer summary (template):
  Subject: Redwood Incident {INC_ID} — Post-incident summary
  Body:
  Hi {CustomerName},

  Summary: What happened, impact, and timeline (one paragraph).
  Root cause: Summary of the root cause and contributing factors.
  Mitigation: Immediate actions we took to stabilize service.
  Next steps: Planned fixes and preventive actions, plus scheduled date for deployment.
  Compensation: If applicable, details on credits and how to claim them.

  Contact: Your account rep or support@redwood.ai

Postmortem template (internal):
- Title: [Postmortem] {INC_ID} — Short description
- Severity: P1 | P2 | P3
- Impact: concise bullet list of affected customers and services
- Timeline: numbered timeline with timestamps and owner at each action
- Root cause analysis: including technical RCA and organizational contributing factors
- Corrective actions (action owner, due date, status)
- Follow-up: postmortem review meeting date, required approvals, communication plan for customers

Game day plan (quarterly):
- Objective: validate runbooks, observe handover friction, and test status-page messaging cadence.
- Duration: 2 hours per simulation (including 30m pre-brief and 30m post-retro).
- Roles: exercise IC (rotating), primary on-call (real responders), Scribe, Customer Success observer, Security rep (when sim includes data concerns).
- Scenario samples: KV cache eviction cascade, noisy neighbor GPU starvation, silent 5xx ramp.
- Success criteria: median MTTR improvement of at least 20% across subsequent two simulations and no major communication delays (>10m between internal declaration and public status).

Runbook governance and review cadence:
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by the owning team and re-approved by Rotation Ops.
- Any runbook changes that affect escalation or customer communication templates require a doll-house test during the next game day.

Appendices:
A) Quick commands and links:
- Incident bridge start: `start-bridge --template SEV2_BRIDGE --title \"{INC_ID} {short-desc}\"`
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/admin (internal)
- Pager tool runbooks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/pd (internal link)

B) Sample NGINX ingress snippet for emergency rate limiting:
```
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=burst_zone:10m rate=40r/s;
server {
  location /v1/generate {
    limit_req zone=burst_zone burst=200 nodelay;
  }
}
```

C) Contact matrix (human-readable):
- Primary on-call: `primary@redwood.ai` (use pager tool for actual paging)
- Secondary: `secondary@redwood.ai`
- Incident Commander rotation: `ic-rotation@redwood.ai`
- Security on-call: `sec-oncall@redwood.ai`
- Customer Success: `cs-incident@redwood.ai`

D) Playbook change log (high level):
- 2025-03-12: Initial draft of rotation policy and SLA Blitz Kit (A. Patel).
- 2026-05-03: Added emergency autoscale commands and quantized-fallback routing (M. Tanaka).
- 2026-11-07: Updated customer templates and quarterly game-day criteria (L. O'Connor).

If you are reading this as a responder: bookmark this page, ensure you have bridge privileges, and follow the first-20-minute checklist immediately on page load. For questions about policy exception or rotation enrollment, contact Rotation Ops at rotation-ops@redwood.ai.
